title: Hom from a locally split lisse sheaf into a flat constructible sheaf
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $U$ a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact). On the small étale site $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] let $A_U$ be the constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and let $E,G$ be sheaves of $A_U$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume:

1. there is an étale covering $\{V_\alpha\to U\}_\alpha$ such that for each $\alpha$ the restriction $E|_{V_\alpha}$ is isomorphic to a direct summand of $A_{V_\alpha}^{\oplus t_\alpha}$ for some finite integer $t_\alpha\geq0$;
2. $G$ is flat, i.e. $-\otimes_{A_U}G$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is exact on $A_U$-module sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf].

Then the sheaf Hom $\mathcal Hom_{A_U}(E,G)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] is a flat and constructible sheaf of $A_U$-modules.

source.place: Proof, Step 2: '(j^*K)^\vee is a bounded complex of constructible flat sheaves' (termwise form of the dual-tensor description of the local Hom)

proof.text: Put $H=\mathcal Hom_{A_U}(E,G)$. On a member $V=V_\alpha$ of the given covering, write $F=A_V^{\oplus t}$ and choose $i:E|_V\to F$, $p:F\to E|_V$ with $pi=1$. By [def-pur-sheaf-hom], precomposition defines $a:H|_V\to\mathcal Hom(F,G|_V)$, $h\mapsto hp$, and $b:\mathcal Hom(F,G|_V)\to H|_V$, $f\mapsto fi$, with $ba=1$. Evaluation on the standard basis identifies $\mathcal Hom(F,G|_V)$ with $(G|_V)^{\oplus t}$. Thus $H|_V$ is the image of the idempotent $e^*:f\mapsto f\circ e$ on this finite sum, where $e=ip$ is an idempotent on $A_V^{\oplus t}$. Each of the finitely many entries of $e$ is a section of $A_V$; [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant], applied to the additive group of $A$, allows a Zariski-open refinement of $V$ on which every entry is constant. On such a piece the matrix is an actual idempotent $e\in\operatorname{Mat}_t(A)$. These refinements still form an étale covering of $U$.

source.place: Proof, Step 2: the termwise local Hom identification from a locally split finite projective term

proof.text: Let $0\to B'\to B\to B''\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $A_U$-module sheaves. On each covering piece $v:V\to U$ of Step 1, restriction is the exact constant-coefficient inverse image of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. That node identifies $v^{-1}A_U$ with $A_V$ and $v^{-1}G$ with the module pullback $v^*G$; hence $G|_V$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-flat-module-pullback]. The restricted tensor sequence for $H$ is the image of the natural idempotent $1\otimes e^*$ on the tensor sequence for $(G|_V)^{\oplus t}$. Restriction commutes with these tensor products: the sectionwise tensor formulas and their covering-local sheafifications in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] are the same on the slice site. The latter sequence is exact because tensoring with $G|_V$ is exact and tensor product distributes over finite sums. The idempotent decomposes each term into its image and kernel, and all sequence maps respect these decompositions. Its image sequence is exact: apply the idempotent to any local lift in the exact sequence to obtain a lift in the image summand. Thus the tensor sequence for $H$ is exact on each $V$. Every geometric point of $U$ lifts to a member of this covering, so exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] shows that its kernel, middle homology, and cokernel have zero stalks. They vanish by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to their maps to zero; kernels and cokernels are those of the abelian module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. This proves flatness as defined in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

source.place: Proof, Step 2: Hom from a locally split finite projective term into a flat sheaf is flat

proof.text: Keep the finite constructible stratification $\iota_k:Z_k\to U$ witnessing constructibility of $G$ in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Base change the covering pieces of Step 1 to $Z_k$ and refine by an étale covering trivializing $\iota_k^{-1}G$ as a finite constant $A$-module $\underline M$. These fibre-product coverings cover $Z_k$ and retain the constant matrix $e$ of Step 1. By exactness and additivity of inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], inverse image of the presentation $H|_V=\operatorname{im}(e^*:(G|_V)^{\oplus t}\to(G|_V)^{\oplus t})$ is $\operatorname{im}(e^*:\underline M^{\oplus t}\to\underline M^{\oplus t})$. This uses an image of a finite-sum endomorphism, not a general assertion that internal Hom commutes with inverse image along a stratum immersion. Let $N=\operatorname{im}(e^*:M^{\oplus t}\to M^{\oplus t})$, where $e^*$ acts by precomposition under $M^{\oplus t}=\operatorname{Hom}_A(A^{\oplus t},M)$. The image sheaf just displayed is $\underline N$: by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant], sections of the constant additive-group sheaves are locally constant functions, and the constant matrix acts pointwise. A locally constant function valued in $N$ locally lifts to a constant element of $M^{\oplus t}$, giving exactly the sheaf image. This identification is $A$-linear. Since $M$ is finite and $t$ is finite, $N$ is finite. Therefore $\iota_k^{-1}H$ is finite locally constant for every $k$, which verifies constructibility of $H$ using the original finite stratification of $G$.

source.place: Proof, Step 2: the termwise Hom sheaf is flat constructible

proof.text: The local identifications in the first step are restrictions of the sheaf $H$ defined by [def-pur-sheaf-hom], so they glue to the stated global sheaf Hom. The second and third steps show respectively that this sheaf is flat and constructible, which is the required conclusion.

On the original constructible stratification of G the constant matrix image is a finite constant module after an étale cover, proving constructibility without a descent claim or new nodes.
